The most dramatic consequence is the stark temperature divide between hemispheres. The dayside, bathed in perpetual starlight, can reach scorching temperatures of hundreds of degrees, while the nightside plunges into deep freeze, potentially cold enough for atmospheric gases to condense and freeze out entirely. Without intervention, this thermal imbalance could cause atmospheric collapse, as gases freeze onto the frozen nightside.
